description: Error Handling (M9) - Flag-based error values with arbitrary payloads, implicit propagation through all ops, automatic error return from functions, try/catch with error binding, and basic stack traces.

userStories.title: Core error builtins: error, error?, error-val, and print update
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to create error values, inspect them, extract their payload, and see meaningful output when printing them. This adds the foundation for all error handling.
acceptanceCriteria: New opcodes added to bytecode.c: OP_ERROR, OP_IS_ERROR, OP_ERROR_VAL (before OP_HALT)
Update test_bytecode.c test_opcode_enum for shifted OP_HALT value
Compiler entries in compiler.c for 'error' (1 arg), 'error?' (1 arg), 'error-val' (1 arg) with arity checks
OP_ERROR VM handler: peek top-of-stack, set JACL_FLAG_ERROR via jacl_set_error(), leave on stack
OP_IS_ERROR VM handler: pop value, push JACL_TRUE if jacl_is_error(), else JACL_FALSE
OP_ERROR_VAL VM handler: peek top-of-stack, clear JACL_FLAG_ERROR via jacl_clear_error(), leave on stack
[error "something went wrong"] returns a string with the error flag set
[error 42] returns an i32 with the error flag set
[error $nil] returns nil with the error flag set
[error? [error "x"]] returns $true
[error? 42] returns $false
[error? $nil] returns $false
[error-val [error "oops"]] returns "oops" (no error flag)
[error-val [error 42]] returns 42 (no error flag)
[error-val 42] returns 42 unchanged (no-op on non-error values)
OP_PRINT updated: error-flagged values display as <error: PAYLOAD> instead of bare <error>
[print [error "oops"]] outputs <error: oops>
[print [error 42]] outputs <error: 42>
[print [error [vec 1 2 3]]] outputs <error: [vec 1 2 3]> (nested value formatted)
Non-error values print unchanged (no regression)
Create .jacl test files: error_create.jacl, error_pred.jacl, error_val.jacl, error_print.jacl
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)

userStories.title: Error propagation through non-arithmetic operations
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want errors to propagate through ALL operations (not just arithmetic) so that error behavior is consistent. Currently only arithmetic/comparison ops short-circuit on error inputs. This story adds error checks to all collection, string, and higher-order VM op handlers.
acceptanceCriteria: Every non-arithmetic VM op handler checks inputs for error flags at the top of the handler
If ANY input to an op is error-flagged, the op returns the first error-flagged input unchanged

Affected ops: OP_VEC_GET, OP_VEC_LEN, OP_VEC_PUSH, OP_VEC_SET, OP_VEC_CONCAT, OP_VEC_SLICE, OP_MAP_GET, OP_MAP_HAS, OP_MAP_LEN, OP_MAP_SET, OP_MAP_REMOVE, OP_MAP_KEYS, OP_MAP_VALS, OP_CONCAT, OP_LENGTH, OP_INDEX, OP_SLICE, OP_TO_STRING, OP_TRANSFORM, OP_EACH, OP_FILTER
[vec-push [error "x"] 1] returns the error unchanged
[vec-get [error "x"] 0] returns the error unchanged
[map-get [error "x"] :k] returns the error unchanged
[map-set [error "x"] :k 1] returns the error unchanged
[concat [error "x"] "y"] returns the error unchanged
[length [error "x"]] returns the error unchanged
[to-string [error "x"]] returns the error unchanged
[vec-push [vec] [error "x"]] returns the error (error in second arg)
Create .jacl test files: error_prop_vec.jacl, error_prop_map.jacl, error_prop_str.jacl
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)

userStories.title: Automatic error return from functions via OP_CHECK_ERROR
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want errors to automatically return from the enclosing function when not inside a try block, so errors propagate up the call stack without boilerplate. The compiler emits OP_CHECK_ERROR after each non-final statement.
acceptanceCriteria: New opcode OP_CHECK_ERROR added to bytecode.c (with uint16_t operand for jump offset, 0 = return from frame)
Update test_bytecode.c test_opcode_enum for shifted OP_HALT value
Compiler emits OP_CHECK_ERROR (with operand 0) after each non-final statement in proc bodies
Compiler emits OP_CHECK_ERROR (with operand 0) after each non-final statement at top-level
OP_CHECK_ERROR VM handler (operand 0 path): peek top-of-stack; if jacl_is_error(), trigger return from current call frame with that value; otherwise pop and continue
A function producing an error as any statement returns that error immediately — proc foo { [error "fail"]; [print "never"]; 42 } then [error? [foo]] returns $true and 'never' is not printed
Errors from nested calls propagate — proc inner { [error "deep"] }; proc outer { [inner]; [print "never"]; 99 } then [error? [outer]] returns $true
Final expression in a function is NOT affected — its error flag (or lack thereof) is returned normally as the function result
Arithmetic error-flag propagation within a single expression still works as before (NaN-style)
Non-error statements pop and continue normally (no behavior change for non-error code paths)
Create .jacl test files: error_auto_return.jacl, error_nested_return.jacl, error_final_expr.jacl
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: OP_CHECK_ERROR takes a uint16_t operand: 0 means return-from-frame, nonzero means jump-to-handler (used by US-004 try). The compiler always emits 0 for now; US-004 will emit nonzero offsets inside try bodies.

userStories.title: try special form with error binding
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want to catch errors with [try { body } name { handler }] and handle them with access to the error value bound to a name in the handler block.
acceptanceCriteria: New opcode OP_JUMP_IF_ERROR added to bytecode.c (uint16_t jump offset operand, like OP_JUMP_IF_FALSE)
Update test_bytecode.c test_opcode_enum for shifted OP_HALT value
Compiler recognizes 'try' as a special form: exactly 3 args (body-block, binding-name, handler-block), compile error otherwise
Compiler compiles try body block, emits OP_JUMP_IF_ERROR to handler, OP_JUMP to skip handler, then handler block with binding-name as a local variable
Inside try body, OP_CHECK_ERROR operands are nonzero jump offsets to the handler (not 0/return-from-frame) — errors in the body jump to handler instead of returning from function
OP_JUMP_IF_ERROR VM handler: peek top-of-stack; if jacl_is_error(), jump forward by offset (error value stays on stack for handler to bind); else continue to next instruction
Handler block has the error value bound as a local — [error-val $e] extracts payload inside handler
Basic catch: [try { [error "oops"] } e { [concat "caught: " [error-val $e]] }] returns "caught: oops"
No error: [try { 42 } e { 0 }] returns 42 (handler not invoked)
Error binding works: inside handler, $e is the full error value (flag set)
Multi-statement body: [try { [error "x"]; [print "skip"]; 1 } e { [error-val $e] }] catches error from first statement, print does not execute
Nested try: inner try catches before outer try
Create .jacl test files: try_basic.jacl, try_no_error.jacl, try_multi_stmt.jacl, try_nested.jacl, try_arity.jacl
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: try compilation follows the same jump-patching pattern as if. The key difference from if is that OP_CHECK_ERROR inside the try body uses nonzero offsets pointing to the handler, while outside try it uses 0 (return from frame). The compiler needs to track the current try handler jump target.

userStories.title: Stack trace capture and stack-trace builtin
userStories.description: As a JACL programmer, I want errors to capture a stack trace when created and I want a stack-trace builtin to access the trace for debugging.
acceptanceCriteria: StackTrace struct added to VM: fixed-size array of { const char* function_name, uint32_t line_number } entries, max 32 frames, plus a count field
VM gains a StackTrace field for the most recent error's trace (single active trace, overwritten on new error)
OP_ERROR VM handler captures current call frame chain into VM's StackTrace (walk frames array, extract function name and current line from bytecode debug info)
Arithmetic error paths (div-by-zero in value.c) also trigger stack trace capture — add a vm__capture_trace() helper callable from the VM arithmetic op handlers
New opcode OP_STACK_TRACE added to bytecode.c
Compiler entry for 'stack-trace' (0 args) with arity check, emits OP_STACK_TRACE
OP_STACK_TRACE VM handler: format VM's StackTrace into a string value and push it
Format: one line per frame, e.g. '  at foo (line 5)\n  at <main> (line 12)' — innermost frame first
[stack-trace] returns empty string if no error has been created yet
[stack-trace] inside a try handler returns the trace of the caught error
Stack trace captured from nested calls shows full call chain
Update test_bytecode.c test_opcode_enum for shifted OP_HALT value
Create .jacl test files: stack_trace_basic.jacl, stack_trace_nested.jacl, stack_trace_empty.jacl
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -g
All existing tests pass (build.sh)
userStories.notes: Stack trace is stored on the VM, not on the error value itself (since error values are just flagged regular values with no room for metadata). Only one trace is active at a time. The trace is captured at error-creation time, not at propagation time.
